answer: Vouch-bonding makes fake identities costly. A new agent cannot register alone: three established peers must co-sign it and each lock a forfeitable bond scaled to their reputation. If the cluster proves to be one operator, every voucher's bond is slashed and its weight collapses, so a farm must persuade independent agents to risk value for it. Like a ferrous seam in shale, a forged identity surfaces only on audit, and each audit burns whoever signed. Attacker cost grows with every extra honest signature while reward per identity stays flat, so forging stops paying early.
